title: Project estimate
headline: Project estimate
subject: Case SAS · member application solution for a standards body, 2018 · RFP stage · no outcome, ever
standfirst: The third case, and the first prepared under the case-profile rule: the team, the site, the domain and the absence of an outcome were pinned before any number existed. The chain was run end to end on one model coordinate; two readings of the outside view were taken in ignorance of it and landed on both sides of it, ×1.8 apart from each other.
meta: chain assembled 8 Sep · outside view read 8 Sep · diagnosed 8 Sep
unit 1 pd = 8 net task hours — leave, holidays and sickness not included

chart.hint:
Two views of the same three distributions. Above, how likely each answer is — all curves on one scale, each enclosing the same area, so the bottom-up looks taller only because its mass is packed into a narrower range. Below, the same thing accumulated: the chance of coming in at or under any figure, which is what a number gets chosen against.

Move the pointer and a read line crosses both panels, reporting the chance of exceeding that figure under each instrument. The two outside-view curves are one sensor run twice on identical input; each declared its own person-month and both are placed by the house factor of 0.75 task hours per recorded hour, which both declarations contain. The calibrated bottom-up sits at about P63 of one reading and above P90 of the other — the diagnosis names that contradiction and does not resolve it. The bottom-up's width is the rate table's optimistic-to-pessimistic spread under a declared ρ = 0.5, scaled by the calibration; it is a convention, not a measurement, and three times narrower than either class reading. Neither reading gave a floor; below P10 each curve is extended to P10²/P50 — the same ratio as P10 to P50 — as a drawing convention, so that the tenth of the mass below P10 is not drawn as a spike. The density panel’s vertical axis reads as chance per 100-pd window; the exact mass is always the cumulative panel.

tiles.d: 57 600 net task hours ≈ 503 staffed person-months. The table-priced assembly of 4765 × the gap-blind Step C chain, ×1.51 — the figure comparable with the outside view.
The drawn band. From the O/M/P in every rate cell, under a declared item correlation of ρ = 0.5, scaled by the calibration.
A different quantity, and not percentiles: the centre at the low and high ends of the Step C rates. 48 100 – 74 100 net task hours.
Two P90s of one sensor that differ ×2: 6270 and 13388 pd. The centre sits at ~P63 of one and above P90 of the other. Nothing averaged.

Two independent size classifications, 85% class agreement, priced from the same table: 38 069 and 38 168 net task hours. Not a measure of precision, the diagnosis says: a symmetric cancellation is the likelier reading.
Two readings of one sensor, in net working time: 215 and 380 person-months in their own declared units. ×1.95 apart after conversion, ×1.77 before it — units explain 4–7% of the gap.

sections.title: How to read the chart
sections.lead: Both instruments produce a distribution. Only one of them did so without being asked.
sections.html:
Both instruments produce a distribution. The outside view produces quantiles natively; the bottom-up's range comes from the optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic value in every rate cell, summed under a declared item correlation of ρ = 0.5 — independent items would claim the total is known to ±1%, perfectly correlated ones would give ×1.9, and the truth is certainly neither. Across ρ from 0.25 to 0.75 the band edges move about ±20%.

The two outside-view readings are one sensor run twice

Same input, same day, same engine. They built the same eight-branch class, excluded the same neighbours, used the same relative anchors — and landed ×1.77 apart at the median before any conversion, because their absolute anchors differ: one staffs the class from tier-1 vendor patterns, the other sizes it in functional units against repository delivery rates. This is the third case on which the class disagrees with itself by more than it disagrees with the chain. Only the marked quantiles are readings; the curve between them is interpolation. Neither reading quoted a P95 — both said the class contains non-delivery beyond P90 and declined to number it, so the tails are hatched rather than drawn.

The unit, and the one conversion applied

Net hours of work on the task, shown as person-days of 8 such hours. Leave, public holidays and sickness are not in these numbers, and neither is any notion of calendar or headcount. Each class reading declared its own unit — 168 recorded hours per person-month with leave outside, and 152 charged hours per person-month with leave inside — and each put its own conversion to task hours in a band containing 0.75. The house factor 0.75 is applied to both, to the class side only; the bottom-up needs none, having been priced in task hours to begin with.

Known direction of error

The bottom-up curve is a normal approximation. Rate cells are right-skewed and correlated sums keep skew, so the true upper tail is fatter than drawn.

sections.title: Why the methods disagree
sections.lead: At equal scope the raw chain sits between the two readings of the outside view; the calibrated centre sits above both. Steps B–D attributed the gaps without closing them, and found the largest one inside the outside view itself.
sections.html:
the class
vs itself
The largest single quantity in the comparison ×1.82
The two outside-view medians are 24 510 and 44 688–47 880 net task hours — three times the distance from the bottom-up to the nearer of them. Before any conversion the raw medians are 215 and 380 person-months, so the conversion did not create it; the two declared units come out within 3% of each other in task hours. Attributed to one free parameter closed two ways: the functional-size regime behind the repository anchor — one reading closed it with a number (1 200–3 000 units × ~12 h), the other with words (“large band, over 1 000 FP”) — plus a staffing anchor about two different crews, plus misclassification leaning opposite ways at equal 60% confidence.
units first
The naive comparison inverts the diagnosis
Number against number, the chain reads 17% above the lower reading and 40% below the higher. After each reading's own declared conversion it is 56% above the lower and 15% below the higher. The direction survives in one case and the magnitude is wrong threefold; in the other, “the instruments nearly agree” would have been a pure artefact of units.
one way
Calibration points up, so it cannot meet both readings
Every Step C correction is upward — the bottom-up's known systematic is omission. Against the higher reading the gap is explained 100% with a +12 900 h overshoot. Against the lower, explained share 0% and the gap widens ×2.43. The class-vs-class gap is addressed by no rate at all. Stated in those words rather than closed by adjustment.
level
The rate table's level round requested
The one uncovered spot that acts multiplicatively on the whole centre. The rate agent spent both permitted globals on sourced effects and refused to touch the table; the diagnostician asks for a narrow gap-blind round on exactly that question and says the centre should be read as “the table's level ×1.50” until it runs.

What Step C adds, and why the rates came out modest

  • T1, T2, T3 — the 31/14 named holes, the real share of ~30 closure violations, and the three coarse XL leaves, each with the structure's own 20% integration on the increment.
  • A-1…A-5 — five once-scoped additions the coverage report itself named as absent: a load test against the five response-time targets, a failover and backup/DR exercise, a WCAG 2.0 A evaluation, a cross-browser matrix, initial help content. 550 / 970 / 1 680 h, the same order as the existing once-scoped layer.
  • G2 ×1.15 — a first-in-domain team, a committee-governed client, generic optimism, merged into one global rather than charged three times.
  • G1 ×1.18 — scope growth: the business rules and the identity protocol the document says will be decided during the project.
  • Suppressed by the coverage report: no integration uplift (paid at 59 parents), no test or rework multiplier (two cycles of each carried), no management, security, environment or documentation uplift. The rate agent called this the largest single effect of the run.

False convergence, checked and refused

The raw chain, 38 118 h, lands within 1.3% of the lower reading's P80 — only at that reading's central conversion factor. At either end of its own declared band the coincidence disappears. The two class readings share an engine, a prompt and a blind-spot list, so their agreement on shape (P90/P50 of 2.24 and 2.05) is reproducibility of one instrument, not independent confirmation; their disagreement on level is a measurement of that instrument's dispersion.

sections.title: Findings
sections.lead: Produced without being asked for, by instruments whose job was something else. The first is the document's own admission; the rest are what the sensors refused to invent.
sections.html:
I-7
The rules the software must obey do not exist yet largest driver, both class readings
“All functionality is validated against X-Customer Standards and business rules, which will be defined as part of the project.” Both outside-view readings, independently, named this the class's characteristic tail: the requirement set moving while it is built. The chain prices elaboration of what is known; the gap-blind scope-growth rate prices the change.
NFR-3 / G-1
Where do users and roles live
One obligation puts accounts and roles in an enterprise identity system whose protocol “has not been finalized”; another puts user administration in the hands of a company administrator inside the application. Reading taken: both, joined by one claims integration.
P-13 / P-14
A stated plurality with no members
“Supported barcodes of various types and sizes” names no symbology. Four were assumed so that the model has something to count; the count is an assumption, declared as one.
A9 · input format
A chain finding, not a document finding
The crossing sensor sees element names, not obligation texts, so the performance-test activity fired on one statement of 24 — the five response-time targets live in the obligation text, which it never received. Named before any number existed; the gap-blind rates later priced the load test as a hole, which is what the record predicted.
MD
What the sensors refused rather than invented
Twenty-five judgement refusals at the crossing, all one question asked twice: does a parent holding only design statements draw test activities, and is a store fed from inside the system a migration target. Three elements refused as too coarse to size (XL) by both sizing repeats: the notification engine, the record import service, the basic-and-full attribute profiles. Catalogue findings, recorded, not repaired.

sections.title: Variant readings
sections.lead: Pinned before any run and consumed by every run. Ask the client; if no answer comes, assume; declare the assumption; and when runs are compared afterwards, exclude the differences the open question causes. All stand unasked here, because this document has no client behind it.

sections.title: Defaults
sections.lead: Each is a fork the document leaves open and the estimate had to close. The reading taken is inside the centre; the reading refused is not.
sections.html:
A4
Identity
Taken: the client's identity system issues claims through one protocol; the application keeps its own company–user–role model and hosts the administration. Refused: all user and role administration inside the identity system, which would reduce three obligations to interface calls.
A6
Import and export worth a branch
Taken: six file formats plus the API, one adapter each; SAP reached through IDoc. Refused: bespoke connectors to named accounting or ERP products — the obligation says “external systems such as QuickBooks or SAP”.
A9
Barcodes and the digital identifier
Taken: four symbologies from a library, at selectable sizes; the embeddable identifier is a snippet with no resolver behind it. Refused: a public resolver service — which the document itself names as future expansion.
A8 · A14
The read store and the reports
Taken: one non-transactional read store fed as changes occur, with reports built into the solution over it. Refused: overnight batch replication; a third-party business-intelligence product. “Near real-time” has no number in the document and none was pinned.
A10
Twenty-five industries
Taken: one configurable mechanism per varying thing, industry parameters as configuration data the client maintains; the industry count multiplies nothing. Refused: industry-specific code paths.
A16 · A17
Migration and environments
Seven entity kinds from the current applications, two rehearsal cycles; four environments, the fourth read as a shared integration environment. The first case in the project to declare migration at all — the sizing sensors split on whether a store written at run time has a migration count, and the catalogue owes an answer.
scope ×2
Two decisions in the technology declaration
One team at one site rather than a distributed delivery (the document names an outsourcing vendor and no site) · an external penetration test and remediation rather than none (nothing in the document names one; three once-scoped items hang on it). Each a declared fork, each separately priceable.
term
Not a default but a hole question for the client
The post-production support period and transition service are carried and not priced: an open-ended obligation has no effort figure until somebody says for how long and at what service level.

sections.title: Estimate gaps
sections.lead: Not oversights. Each is a thing the chain refused to price, with the reason it refused.
sections.html:
1
The post-production support period awaiting a parameter
Carried on every side, awaiting the term and the service level. All three instruments exclude it consistently; no double count. The one-sided risk that the class anchors hold a warranty period inside the team's tenure is named and unpriced.
2
The refused readings
Administration inside the identity system · product connectors to accounting and ERP systems · a public resolver · industry-specific code paths · a business-intelligence product · a distributed delivery · no penetration test. Each a step change, not a multiplier; not in the centre, and not priced as options on this case — no step-event round was run.
3
The rate table's level
Uncalibrated against any outcome. A narrow gap-blind round is requested, not run. Until then the centre is the table's level raised ×1.50, not an independent statement about effort.
4
The era
Eight years between the document and the norms. Three independent instruments refused to adjust, for the same reason: tooling pulls down, expectations on security, accessibility and operability pull up, and no source decides which wins.
5
Tail and failure events
A late or changed identity platform, business rules never defined, committee stalemate, migration data that cannot be reconciled. Inside the class quantiles, in no bottom-up item — hence in the reserve and nowhere else.
6
Effort to calendar, and team availability
A separate step, deliberately. Task hours do not become dates without a team shape, and this report supplies no team shape.

sections.title: Where every number came from
sections.lead: Each sensor is an engine with a version, stamped on its own output. They are hired for what they are forbidden to see, not for autonomy.
sections.html:
1
Product model · n = 2
146 product obligations → 246 elements (the second reading: 242, anchored structure ×1.017). Produces no effort figure of any kind. Both replies lost their head in transit — a protocol fact on record, not a repair.
2
Work model
Crossed against a declared technology, seven batches → 1 650 work items on 245 elements. May not invent an activity: work the product needs but no declared activity covers is reported as a finding — 25 such refusals here.
3
Size classes · n = 2
Each of 187 elements classified by counting named things, the enumeration being the justification. Refuses to run if shown any rate or price. Class agreement 85.0%; whole-chain repeat spread ×1.0026.
4
Rate table uncalibrated
External norms in net task hours, gap-blind: never saw a project total, a budget, or a gap a rate would explain. Calibrated against no outcome — the centre is norms passed through a measured size vector, not a validated cost.
5
Outside view ×2
Ran in parallel and in ignorance of all of the above, the unit convention withheld so that each declared its own. Both quarantined the repository status the harness prepends, naming the numeric commit subject in it without using it.
6
Steps B, C, D
Calibration parameters from a gap-blind source that never saw the outside view or the size of the gap; then the diagnosis, the only participant permitted to see more than one method's output — told in its brief that no outcome exists.

Two coordinates, not one

An estimate is a property of the triple (project × engine × model). Every sensor on this case ran on the same model, Claude Opus 5, so the model coordinate is held fixed and the readings above are engine-and-project readings only.

The declaration is required, not volunteered

Every role that produces a number must state, before any figure, its unit, whether leave sits inside it, whose roles are counted, and how far its own sources disagree. This case is the first on which two readings of one sensor declared different units — 168 recorded hours per person-month with leave outside, 152 charged hours with leave inside — which is exactly what requiring the declaration was for.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.lead: This report is one output of a method that is written down. Nothing below is specific to this case; every file states what it is for, what it may not do, and what would change it.
sections.html:
frame
METHODOLOGY.md
Why independence of techniques replaces independence of experts, what each method is structurally blind to, and why a divergence is diagnosed rather than averaged.
chain
docs/instrument.md
What actually runs: the product model, the crossing against a declared technology, the size classes, the pinned table, the script. What is pinned at each step and what each sensor is forbidden to produce.
numbers
docs/constants.md
Every constant the method has, and the comparison-layer conversion pinned by the author: 6 net task hours per present day, ×1.10 leave, 21 days — so 1 staffed person-month ≈ 114.5 net task hours.
case
docs/case_profile.md
The rule this case was the first to follow: team grade, site count, domain familiarity and the outcome's unit are pinned before any estimate exists, so that no condition can be chosen after a number is on the table.
isolation
PIPELINE.md
The visibility matrix: who may see what, in what order the sensors are launched, and the disciplines that are mechanically checkable rather than promised.
prices
docs/rate_table.md · technology_catalogue.md
The pinned rates, in net person-hours, written gap-blind by a role that never saw a project total. And the vocabulary a technology declaration is written in — this case's declaration proposes one amendment to it.
done
docs/exit_criterion.md
When the instrument may be called fit for use, decided in advance. This case scores repeatability and, given a human scale, position; it cannot score calibratability, because it has no outcome.
this case
examples/SAS/
The pinned inputs, the case profile, the assumption log, the technology declaration, and every run with its raw sensor output kept verbatim.

fine: What this report is not. Not a validated price, and not a price at all — it is work content in net task hours, shown as person-days of eight such hours. Converting it into money, calendar or headcount is the reader's act, using the reader's own figures. Every bottom-up number rests on a rate table of external industry norms calibrated against no outcome; the bottom-up stands on one product model of two; and this case has no outcome and never will, so nothing here has been checked against reality.

What it is. The estimate, its corridor, the disagreement between two structurally independent methods stated rather than averaged away — here, chiefly the disagreement of the outside view with itself — and, on the record, the obligations, the findings, the questions and the defaults that the number is standing on.
